text:
Let your AI agents use your real browser: your tabs, your logins, your extensions. A small native MCP server and a
Chromium extension, for OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and any other MCP client.

---

Agents get a browse MCP server. They open tabs in the background, read pages, click, type, take screenshots,
capture network traffic and record the screen, in tabs grouped out of your way. When it's your turn (a login, a 2FA
prompt, a payment), they hand the tab back to you and continue once you click Continue .

It works in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Helium, Vivaldi, Opera and Chromium.

 Install

 

Or paste this into your agent: "Set up browse so you can use my Chrome: run
 curl -fsSL bash " . It sets browse up for the agent that ran it.

Other ways to install, all of which end in the same browse install :

 How Command Where browse lives, and what updates it 
 --- --- --- 
 Install script (macOS, Linux) curl -fsSL \ bash /.local/bin/browse ( $XDG BIN HOME when set); updates itself 
 Install script (Windows) irm \ iex in PowerShell %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\browse.exe ; updates itself 
 npx, bunx npx @opencode/browse install copied to /.local/bin/browse once; updates itself from then on 
 npm npm i -g @opencode/browse , then browse install npm's global browse ; browse runs npm install -g to update 
 bun bun add -g @opencode/browse , then browse install /.bun/bin/browse ; browse runs bun add -g to update 
 pnpm, yarn, volta pnpm add -g / yarn global add / volta install @opencode/browse , then browse install that manager's browse ; updated with the same manager 

There's always exactly one browse : a global package install is left to its package manager (nothing is copied next
to it, and a leftover /.local/bin/browse from an earlier install is removed), and agents run the same browse your
terminal does. If browse install finds another browse on your PATH it tells you which one and how to remove it.

The install script reads the channel's manifest from Anomaly's release service, downloads
the binary for this computer and checks its size and SHA-256 before installing it. --channel stable beta dev picks
the channel ( stable by default); --version installs a specific version from npm, checked against npm's
published SHA-512 integrity. With npm, @opencode/browse@dev is the dev channel. The npm package is a small Node
launcher (Node 22+) that runs the native binary npm installed for your platform.

 What browse install does

1. Puts browse in place (see above) and adds /.local/bin to your PATH when it copied browse there
 ( --no-modify-path skips that).
2. Adds the browse MCP server to your agents. In a terminal you get a picker: OpenCode and the agents found on this
 computer start checked (your last choice next time). Type to search all supported agents, ↑/↓ to move, Space or Tab
 to toggle, Enter to confirm. An agent running browse install sets up itself. Without a terminal OpenCode is the
 default. Edits keep the comments and formatting of each agent's config, and a config that's a symlink (a
 dotfiles repo, Nix Home Manager) stays one: browse writes the file it points at.
3. Connects the extension. If no browser has browse yet, install opens it in the Chrome Web Store; add it, and
 install pairs it once it's there. If a browser already has it, install opens its setup page with a one-time pairing
 code in the link, so it pairs without copying anything. Over SSH or without a display it prints a code instead.

Then ask your agent to "open news.ycombinator.com and tell me the top story" . An agent that was already running
needs a restart (or an MCP reload) to load browse.

 

 Supported agents and their user-level config files 

 CONFIG is $XDG CONFIG HOME or /.config . APP is /Library/Application Support on macOS, %APPDATA% on

install.title: Install
install.html:
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/browse/install | bash

Or paste this into your agent: "Set up browse so you can use my Chrome: run curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/browse/install | bash". It sets browse up for the agent that ran it.

Other ways to install, all of which end in the same browse install:

How Command Where browse lives, and what updates it
Install script (macOS, Linux) curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/browse/install | bash ~/.local/bin/browse ($XDG_BIN_HOME when set); updates itself
Install script (Windows) irm https://opencode.ai/browse/install.ps1 | iex in PowerShell %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\browse.exe; updates itself
npx, bunx npx @opencode/browse install copied to ~/.local/bin/browse once; updates itself from then on
npm npm i -g @opencode/browse, then browse install npm's global browse; browse runs npm install -g to update
bun bun add -g @opencode/browse, then browse install ~/.bun/bin/browse; browse runs bun add -g to update
pnpm, yarn, volta pnpm add -g / yarn global add / volta install @opencode/browse, then browse install that manager's browse; updated with the same manager

There's always exactly one browse: a global package install is left to its package manager (nothing is copied next to it, and a leftover ~/.local/bin/browse from an earlier install is removed), and agents run the same browse your terminal does. If browse install finds another browse on your PATH it tells you which one and how to remove it.

The install script reads the channel's manifest from Anomaly's release service, downloads the binary for this computer and checks its size and SHA-256 before installing it. --channel stable|beta|dev picks the channel (stable by default); --version <version> installs a specific version from npm, checked against npm's published SHA-512 integrity. With npm, @opencode/browse@dev is the dev channel. The npm package is a small Node launcher (Node 22+) that runs the native binary npm installed for your platform.

What browse install does
  1. Puts browse in place (see above) and adds ~/.local/bin to your PATH when it copied browse there (--no-modify-path skips that).
  2. Adds the browse MCP server to your agents. In a terminal you get a picker: OpenCode and the agents found on this computer start checked (your last choice next time). Type to search all supported agents, ↑/↓ to move, Space or Tab to toggle, Enter to confirm. An agent running browse install sets up itself. Without a terminal OpenCode is the default. Edits keep the comments and formatting of each agent's config, and a config that's a symlink (a dotfiles repo, Nix Home Manager) stays one: browse writes the file it points at.
  3. Connects the extension. If no browser has browse yet, install opens it in the Chrome Web Store; add it, and install pairs it once it's there. If a browser already has it, install opens its setup page with a one-time pairing code in the link, so it pairs without copying anything. Over SSH or without a display it prints a code instead.

Then ask your agent to "open news.ycombinator.com and tell me the top story". An agent that was already running needs a restart (or an MCP reload) to load browse.

browse install -a claude codex   # these agents, without asking (--agent; names below)
browse install -a '*'            # every supported agent, installed or not
browse install -y                # every agent found on this computer
browse install --agent none      # no agent: print the MCP entry to add by hand

usage.title: Using it
usage.html:
• Tabs are the handle. navigate without a tab opens a new background tab and returns its id; every other call passes that tab. Agents use the tab ids they opened or were given, and leave other tabs alone unless you ask. Tabs can be opened with options that stick: group (the tab group's title, and a handle to close them together), allowedOrigins, readOnly, keepVisible, keepOpen (never close it as idle) and browser. Popups a page opens become agent tabs too.
  • Tabs keep their ids, and an agent can name one. tabs with action: "new" and an id like work-mail opens that tab once: asking again returns the same tab without navigating it, and every tool takes work-mail as tab. The id lasts while the tab stays open: a relay restart or extension reload keeps it, and a browser restart loses it (opening that id again is a fresh tab). tabs lists each tab's id, url, title, group, last use, whether a call is running in it, the browser window it's in, and a waiting handoff's message. A tab opened with keepOpen: true stays until an agent or you close it; every other tab closes when idle like the rest. keepOpen needs extension 0.1.2 or newer: an older one can't hold a tab open, so it still closes when idle and browse tells the agent.
  • A task keeps to its window. A new tab with a group label opens in the window where that label's tabs are, in either window setting, so if you move a task's tabs to a window of their own, its next tabs open there too (when they're split across windows, the one you used last; the agent is told so it can ask you). An agent can also open a task in a new background window (newWindow) or in the window of a tab it names (windowOf); neither changes your window setting. OPENCODE_BROWSER_AGENT_WINDOW fixes placement, so labels don't move tabs while it's set.
  • Agents open their own tabs in the background of the window you last used, grouped together and collapsed unless you're looking at one (you can turn that off). By default, agents can't switch you to their tabs or bring a window to the front. A relay started with OPENCODE_BROWSER_ALLOW_FOREGROUND=1 lets page.bringToFront() in execute raise the tab and its window. Tabs nobody touches for 10 minutes close by themselves, or whatever idle close is set to below (never while something runs on them). Closing agent tabs never quits the browser or leaves it without a window: browse leaves a new tab (or window) behind when it would close the last one.
  • Relay restarts keep agent tabs. The relay saves the tabs agents opened and their options, and takes them back when it starts again (after an update, say).
  • Hand an agent one of your tabs by clicking the toolbar button on it. The badge shows ON; click again to take it back. While an agent works the badge reads RUN, and WAIT when it needs you. The button always works: a click while an agent runs takes the tab back. The browser's debugging bar (Cancel, or OK in some browsers) disconnects browse from every tab; browse shows a notification when that happens, and clicking the browse button on a tab lends it again. Chrome's own pages, the Web Store included, can't be lent.
  • Handoffs: the page shows a small card with the site's origin. Do the human part, then click Continue on the card or the toolbar button. While a tab is recorded you get a system notification instead of the card.
  • Uploads. Large files, or sites that reject copied files, work when the browser is on the same computer and the extension has "Allow access to file URLs" turned on in the browser's extensions page (browse → Details): that lets the extension read files on this computer, and browse only hands it files from its file roots. Otherwise browse copies the files in, up to 50 MB per call. Files that aren't on the relay's machine can be passed inline as base64 ({ name, data }): those always copy in and fit about 10 MB per call (the 50 MB limit is for paths copied in), and mixing them with paths copies the paths in too.
  • Several browsers at once. Each connected browser has an id (like chrome-macbook); status lists them, and new tabs open in the default browser unless browser names another. The id comes from the browser's name, or the name set in the extension's settings. Helium tells extensions it is Chrome, so a browser on this computer that says it is Chrome is named Helium (helium-macbook) when Helium has browse and no other browser here that could say "Chrome" does. When browse can't tell, a browser already named Helium keeps its name and id. A Chrome browse can't see (a custom profile folder, say) next to Helium may be named Helium too: set a name for it in the extension's settings.
  • Settings (the extension's options page, applied right away): where agent tabs open (your window or their own), grouping (one shared group, one per task, or none), whether browse collapses agent groups by itself or leaves them as you set them (a handoff still opens its group so you can find the tab), when idle tabs close (10, 30, 60 minutes or never), whether agent tabs open muted, human-like input, and handoff notifications. Agents can read and change these with the settings tool when you ask them to.
  • Labs (under labs on the options page, each off until you turn it on): experimental features. Save pages as PDF gives agents the pdf tool and page.pdf() in execute. Restart your agent after turning one on so it sees the new tool. Labs features only work in browsers that have the browse extension.
